title: Linux at Long Last + GPLv3
excerpt: Obscura is now available as a native app on Linux, with official packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch
content_html:
TL;DR

  • Obscura VPN is now available on Linux
  • We’re offering 25% off to all users with promo code LINUX26
  • Official packages for: Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch and their derivatives
  • Obscura is now licensed under GPLv3

Today, Obscura finally comes to Linux.

Obscura’s code has been public since day one, and we believe the future of an open and private internet starts with open source.

We’re releasing the Obscura Linux app with a full graphical interface alongside an experimental command-line interface.

Launch Offer: 25% Off for All Users

Penguins of the world, rejoice, as part of our launch we’re giving everyone 25% off (for a limited time). Use promo code LINUX26 at checkout to claim your discount.

Supported Distros

We’re offering official packages for the following Linux distros:

  • Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, and other derivatives
  • Fedora, RHEL, Silverblue, and other derivatives
  • Arch Linux, CachyOS, Omarchy, and other derivatives

If your distro is based on any of these, you’re covered.

Don’t see your favorite distro here? Tweet us at @obscuravpn or email support@obscura.net to let us know which distro we should support next.

Obscura is Now Licensed Under GPLv3

We’re relicensing from the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 to the GNU General Public License v3.0 furthering our commitment to Open Source software.

Thanks to Rowan Comish, John Meza and Carl Dong for reading drafts of this.
